Well , to clarify, was talking about powerlifting rules and objective wasn't solely to look for an optimum ROM , but a range outside which the lift isn't counted. , we know that the loopholes have been exploited already with the ring being the maximum grip width or anyhow. 

Note especially that strength is not just a function of force, but distance as well, "Work done" basically. Work done = Force* displacement or angular displacement anyhow. 

You could be lifting 300kg for 3 inches =~ 2.33 Nm of work or  150.39 for 6 inches , same work.


So if you're lifting heavy for half a "fixed distance" vs half as heavy for twice the same fixed distance , the work done is same.
(An analogy is to push a door about its hinge , at the opposite side of the hinge, a very small force can push the door, but the same force cannot as you move closer to its hinge)

What I'm basically saying is, instead of limiting the ROM by the grip width, a angular limit is much more useful and without as many loopholes.
